correctness.rationale: A fresh independent recursion enumerated all 272 labeled perfect matchings of Q4 and tested all 24 coordinate squares, recovering exactly 768 flip edges, eight frozen matchings and one 264-state mobile component. The eight frozen Q4 bases each have exactly three edge-disjoint alternative frozen neighbors; the frozen-edge-disjointness relation is two copies of K4, as shown by the computed degree-3 mutually disjoint blocks. For Q5, the submitted 120 frozen among 589185 total matches the earlier complete published Q5 census, which was read in full; this finite result is already known. For general d>=5, decompose Q_d=Q4 Cartesian Q_{d-4}: all even-parity layers carry one fixed frozen Q4 matching; independently select in each odd layer one of three edge-disjoint alternatives. Internal squares cannot flip; cross-layer squares cannot have both parallel dimers because adjacent-layer matchings are edge-disjoint, and squares in layer directions have no dimers. There are 2^{d-5} odd layers and 8 disjoint even-base choices, proving 8*3^{2^{d-5}} frozen matchings for all d. The all-dimensional bound is an analytical constructive proof, not a Q5 extrapolation.

evidence: Earlier Q5 full component census strengthens submitted Q5 isolated count; higher-dimensional connectivity under *longer* alternating-cycle moves uses a more permissive adjacency.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Q5 complete theorem dominates finite Q5 part, but its fixed dimension does not imply F_d >= 8*3^{2^{d-5}} for every d>=5. Longer-cycle update connectivity does not imply no square flip in the present model.
